questions.question: What is the name of the tiny air sacs that make up the structure of human lungs?
options: Bronchioles
Alveoli
Tracheoles
Capillaries

questions.question: Why does the human lung contain millions of tiny alveoli instead of just a few large sacs?
options: To reduce the physical weight of the lungs
To increase the temperature of the inhaled air
To increase the surface area available for gas exchange
To prevent dust from entering the bloodstream

questions.question: How does the thickness of the alveolar walls benefit the process of gas exchange?
options: They are several cells thick to prevent damage
They are one cell thick to minimize the diffusion distance
They are one cell thick to increase the temperature of gases
They are several cells thick to filter out pathogens

questions.question: Which chemical substance is absolutely required for aerobic cellular respiration to take place?
options: Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Ethanol
Oxygen

questions.question: In which parts of animal, plant, and fungi cells does aerobic cellular respiration take place?
options: Chloroplasts and cell wall
Nucleus and vacuole
Mitochondria and cytoplasm
Ribosomes and cell membrane

questions.question: Muscle cells require a lot of energy to perform physical work. How does their structure adapt to this need?
options: They lack cytoplasm entirely
They contain a larger number of mitochondria
They have fewer mitochondria to conserve space
They have a single, massive chloroplast

questions.question: What are the products of anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms such as yeast?
options: Lactic acid and oxygen
Glucose and water
Carbon dioxide and lactic acid
Carbon dioxide and ethanol

questions.question: What is another common term used for anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms?
options: Fermentation
Photosynthesis
Transpiration
Combustion

questions.question: What product is formed during anaerobic cellular respiration in humans that can cause muscle cramps?
options: Ethanol
Carbon dioxide
Lactic acid
Glucose

questions.question: Where in a cell does anaerobic cellular respiration take place?
options: Only in the cytoplasm, without involving the mitochondria
Only in the mitochondria, without involving the cytoplasm
In both the nucleus and the ribosomes
In the chloroplasts of animal cells

questions.question: How does anaerobic cellular respiration compare to aerobic cellular respiration in terms of energy release?
options: It provides more energy, but provides it more slowly
It provides less energy, but provides it more quickly
It provides the same amount of energy at the exact same speed
It provides more energy and provides it more quickly

questions.question: What is the primary physical purpose of breathing in humans and other animals?
options: To chemically break down glucose in cells
To pump blood through the capillaries
To move air into and out of the lungs
To produce lactic acid in the muscles

questions.question: During the process of gas exchange in the human body, how do gases move?
options: Oxygen diffuses from lungs to blood; carbon dioxide diffuses from blood to lungs
Oxygen diffuses from blood to lungs; carbon dioxide diffuses from lungs to blood
Both oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse from lungs to blood
Both oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse from blood to lungs

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about cellular respiration in living organisms?
options: It occurs only in animals when they are physically active
It occurs only in plants during the nighttime
It occurs in all living organisms all the time to keep them alive
It occurs only in microorganisms during fermentation

questions.question: What is defined as the vital capacity of the lungs?
options: The total amount of air left in the lungs after a normal exhalation
The volume of oxygen consumed by cells during one minute of rest
The amount of carbon dioxide produced in a single breath
The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after inhaling fully

questions.question: In scientific measurements, what does it mean if a measured value is said to be highly accurate?
options: It is very close to the true value of the quantity
It is written down with many decimal places
It was estimated without using any equipment
It is different every time the measurement is repeated

questions.question: How do muscles assist in the mechanism of breathing to move air into the lungs?
options: They contract to change the volume and pressure in the chest cavity
They directly push air molecules into the bloodstream
They contract to squeeze the alveoli shut
They relax to allow the trachea to expand and contract
